spatialPresets.description: Manual configuration recipes for FLEX's Delay and Reverb modules to create specific spatial environments. Apply these settings to the bottom FX row.

spaces.name: Intimate Studio Room
spaces.description: A tight, controlled space that adds dimension without being 'reverby'.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Natural ambience, minimal reflections, preserved transients
tips: Perfect for lead vocals that need to sit up front
Increase Mix to 18-20% for background vocals
common_mistakes: Adding delay on top - it clutters the space
Using this on bass - bass should stay dry

spaces.name: Massive Valhalla Hall
spaces.description: Huge, lush, long-tail reverb for epic scale.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Endless decay, cathedral-like depth, lush and immersive
tips: Perfect for epic builds and breakdowns
Automate the reverb mix from 30% to 60% during builds
Works great with long Attack envelopes (1-2s)
common_mistakes: Using this on busy elements - it will muddy the mix
Forgetting to sidechain compress against kick/snare

spaces.name: Slapback Rock
spaces.description: Vintage 50s/60s echo effect. Distinct single repeat.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Short, single distinct echo like vintage tape delay
tips: Classic on rockabilly and surf guitar
Try 80-120ms range to taste
Keep feedback low - you want ONE clear repeat
common_mistakes: Using tempo-synced time - ruins the vintage feel
Adding too much reverb - defeats the tight character

spaces.name: Underwater Ambience
tips: Combine with Master Filter Low Pass at 2-4kHz for deeper submersion
Works great with long Attack envelopes
Perfect for transitional textures
common_mistakes: Not cutting enough highs - keeps it too clear
Using this on lead elements - they'll disappear

spaces.name: Rhythmic Ghost
spaces.description: Creates a rhythmic backdrop behind the main sound.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Bouncing stereo delays that create polyrhythmic texture
tips: Perfect for house and techno plucks
Try 3/8 for slower, spacier feel
Automate feedback for build-ups
common_mistakes: Too much feedback - creates chaos
Using on bass - muddies low end

spaces.name: Dry Studio (Minimal Processing)
spaces.description: Ultra-dry with just a hint of space for natural sound.
tips: Perfect for modern hip-hop and trap vocals
Keeps vocals cutting through dense beats
Add 10-15ms pre-delay for more separation (if FLEX supports it)
common_mistakes: Going completely 0% reverb - sounds unnatural
Using the same setting for background vocals

spaces.name: Dub Echo Chamber
spaces.description: Classic reggae/dub delay with heavy feedback and filtering.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Trippy, infinite echoes, progressively darker repeats
tips: Automate delay feedback from 0% to 85% for classic dub effects
Use on send track for more control
Combine with Limiter set to 'Warming' for analog character
common_mistakes: Not automating - static dub echo is boring
Feedback above 85% - creates runaway feedback

spaces.name: Stereo Widener (Haas Effect)
spaces.description: Uses ultra-short delays to widen mono sounds without reverb.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Wide stereo image, maintains clarity, no wetness
tips: Perfect for synths that need width without losing focus
Keep delay time under 30ms to avoid audible echo
Check mono compatibility - may cause phase issues
common_mistakes: Using on bass - destroys mono compatibility
Delay time too long - creates audible slap
Combining with wide unison - gets too wide

spaces.name: Plate Reverb (Vintage)
spaces.description: Simulates classic EMT plate reverb - bright and dense.
spaces.audio_characteristics: Dense, bright, metallic shimmer, short-to-medium decay
tips: Classic on snares and vocals
Increase Color to 85%+ for '80s snare sound
Works great with Limiter set to 'Warming'
common_mistakes: Too much size - loses the 'plate' character
Using on bass or low instruments

spaces.name: Spring Reverb (Surf)
spaces.description: Emulates vintage spring reverb tanks found in guitar amps.
tips: High mod rate simulates spring wobble
Keep decay short for authentic sound
Combine with Slapback Rock delay for surf guitar
common_mistakes: Making decay too long - real springs are short
Not enough mod - loses the characteristic wobble

combination_tips: Intimate Studio Room + Slapback Rock = Modern country vocal
Massive Valhalla Hall + Rhythmic Ghost = Trance lead
Dry Studio + Stereo Widener = Modern trap vocal
Dub Echo Chamber + Underwater Ambience = Experimental ambient
automation_ideas: Automate reverb mix from 0% to 60% during breakdowns
Automate delay feedback from 30% to 85% for dub effects
Automate reverb color from 20% to 80% for evolving textures
Automate delay time (if possible) for pitch-shift effects

envelopeShapes.description: Standard ADSR (Attack, Hold, Decay, Sustain, Release) configurations for common sound types. Apply these to the Volume Envelope sliders in FLEX.

envelope_basics.Attack: Time from 0% to 100% volume after key press
envelope_basics.Hold: Time at 100% volume before decay starts
envelope_basics.Decay: Time from 100% down to Sustain level
envelope_basics.Sustain: Volume level held while key is pressed
envelope_basics.Release: Time from current level to 0% after key release

shapes.name: Sharp Pluck
shapes.description: Immediate impact with no sustain. Sounds like a string being plucked.

common_problems.solution: Increase Release to 20-30%
Increase Attack slightly to 2-5%

shapes.velocity_interaction: High velocity should trigger brighter tone - check if Macro controls velocity sensitivity
mix_tips: Layer with longer release for sustained chords

shapes.name: Atmospheric Pad
shapes.description: Slow fade-in and long fade-out. No sudden movements.

common_problems.symptom: Takes too long to hear the sound
common_problems.solution: Reduce Attack to 40-50%
Use High Pass filter or reduce Release to 50%

shapes.velocity_interaction: Low velocity sensitivity - pads should be consistent
mix_tips: Layer multiple instances with different Attack times

shapes.name: Punchy Bass / 808
shapes.description: Hard hit that sustains fully, but stops immediately when key is released (to avoid mud).

common_problems.symptom: Bass notes run into each other
common_problems.solution: Reduce Release to 3-5%
Increase Attack to 2-3%
Increase Release to 12-15%

shapes.velocity_interaction: Should respond to velocity for dynamic expression
mix_tips: Sidechain to kick for cleaner mix

shapes.name: Orchestral Strings (Legato)
shapes.description: Natural bow movement. Not instant, but not a slow pad.
shapes.sound_character: Natural, organic swell, realistic bow articulation

common_problems.solution: Add slight random variation to Attack times (layer multiple instances)
Increase Release or use portamento/glide

shapes.velocity_interaction: Critical - high velocity = louder and brighter
mix_tips: Layer with different velocities for depth

shapes.name: Percussive Hit / Stab
shapes.description: One-shot sound. Key hold duration doesn't matter.

common_problems.solution: Increase Decay and Release to 60-80%
Reduce Release to 20-30%

shapes.name: Smooth Organ
shapes.description: Instant on, instant off. Like turning a switch.

common_problems.solution: Add minimal Attack (2-3%)
Increase Release to 8-10%

mix_tips: Add rotary speaker effect for authentic sound

shapes.name: Piano (Acoustic)
shapes.description: Fast attack with long, natural decay that fades out even while held.
shapes.sound_character: Natural piano decay, percussive start, long tail

common_problems.solution: Increase Sustain to 50-60%
Reduce Sustain to 20-30%

shapes.velocity_interaction: Critical for expressiveness - map velocity to filter and volume

shapes.name: Brass Swell
shapes.description: Medium attack with full sustain - mimics breath control.
shapes.sound_character: Breath-like swell, powerful sustain, controlled release

common_problems.symptom: Attack too slow for fast passages
common_problems.solution: Create separate preset with Attack at 10-15%
Automate Macro 1 for vibrato/expression

shapes.velocity_interaction: High velocity = louder and brighter brass tone
mix_tips: Medium reverb with natural room sound
Layer multiple takes for section sound

shapes.name: Synthesizer Lead (Short)
shapes.description: Fast attack, short decay - aggressive and cutting.

common_problems.solution: Reduce Release to 10%
Increase Sustain to 70%

mix_tips: Use Ping Pong delay for width

shapes.name: Synthesizer Lead (Long)
shapes.description: Medium attack with long sustain - soaring and epic.

common_problems.solution: Reduce Attack to 20-25%
Reduce Release to 30-35%

envelope_application_tips: Start with a preset close to your target sound
Adjust one parameter at a time and listen
Use automation clips to vary envelopes over time
Check envelope behavior at different velocities

genre_specific_approaches.EDM: Fast attacks, medium releases - keep it punchy
genre_specific_approaches.Ambient: Long attacks and releases - create evolving textures
genre_specific_approaches.Hip-Hop: Sharp attacks, short releases - tight and controlled
genre_specific_approaches.Classical: Natural attacks and releases - mimic real instruments
genre_specific_approaches.Trap: Instant attacks, varies releases - bass short, leads medium

genreTemplates.description: Recommended starting points for FLEX settings based on musical genre. Use these as a checklist when initializing a new patch.
how_to_use: 1. Load a FLEX preset from the recommended packs
2. Apply the macro suggestions from the genre template
3. Configure the FX chain as specified
4. Fine-tune envelope settings for your specific sound
5. Remember: these are starting points, not rules

genres.name: Cinematic / Score
genres.key_characteristics: Epic scale, emotional depth, dynamic range

macro_suggestions.Timbre: Start low (30%), open to 80% during climax

mixing_tips: Automate reverb mix during swells (20% to 60%)
Use sidechain on pads when strings enter
common_mistakes: Too much compression - kills dynamics
Not enough automation - sounds static
Reverb too short - loses epic scale

genres.name: Deep House
genres.key_characteristics: Deep basslines, warm chords, soulful vocals, jazzy elements
mixing_tips: Add vintage warmth with Limiter 'Warming' mode
common_mistakes: Bass too wide - causes phase issues
Too bright - loses warmth
Too much reverb on bass

genres.name: Techno / Industrial
genres.key_characteristics: Repetitive elements, dark atmosphere, heavy bass, industrial textures

fx_chain.Master_Filter: Automate Low Pass or High Pass

common_mistakes: Too many elements - loses hypnotic quality
Reverb too bright
Not enough automation

genres.name: Dubstep / Riddim
genres.key_characteristics: Heavy wobble bass, aggressive modulation, sparse arrangement, sub focus
mixing_tips: Keep sub separate from mid bass
common_mistakes: Sub bass not mono
Too much reverb on bass
Static wobbles - needs automation

genres.name: Trance / Uplifting
genres.key_characteristics: Soaring leads, lush pads, arpeggiated plucks, emotional breakdowns
common_mistakes: Not enough reverb - loses epic scale
Static leads - needs modulation
Too muddy - high-pass pads

genres.name: Drum & Bass
genres.key_characteristics: Fast breakbeats, heavy sub bass, complex rhythms, atmospheric pads

fx_chain.Master_Filter: High Pass for pads to clear bass space

mixing_tips: Sub bass must be mono and clean
Heavy sidechain on everything except sub
common_mistakes: Sub bass too wide
Too much processing on bass
Not enough space for drums

genres.name: Future Bass
genres.key_characteristics: Bright supersaws, vocal chops, dynamic drops, emotional melodies
common_mistakes: Not enough unison/detune
Too dark - needs brightness
Static - needs constant movement

genres.name: R&B / Neo-Soul
genres.key_characteristics: Smooth chords, warm bass, soulful keys, subtle textures
common_mistakes: Too bright - loses soul
Over-processing - loses organic feel
Not enough warmth

cross_genre_tips: Always start with envelope settings that match the genre's energy
Reverb decay time should match tempo (faster BPM = shorter decay)
Aggressive genres benefit from Limiter 'Distortion' mode
Emotional genres need long attacks and releases
Electronic genres use more automation than organic genres

dynamicsPresets.description: Recipes for the Limiter section (Bottom Right) to achieve different dynamic characters and saturation colors.

limiter_types_explained.Limiter: Clean, transparent peak limiting - no coloration
limiter_types_explained.Warming: Soft-knee compression with mild saturation - analog warmth
limiter_types_explained.Heating: Harder compression with noticeable saturation - aggressive
limiter_types_explained.Distortion: Hard clipping and overdrive - heavy coloration
limiter_types_explained.Custom: Preset-defined curve - varies by sound designer

presets.name: Transparent Safety
presets.description: Catches peaks without coloring the sound. Default behavior.
presets.sonic_character: Invisible limiting, maintains dynamic range, no harmonics added
when_to_use: When you need peak protection only
tips: Increase Pre slightly (5-10%) if preset is too quiet
This is the default for a reason - start here

presets.name: Analog Warmth
presets.description: Subtle saturation that thickens the sound, similar to tube gear.
presets.sonic_character: Warm, slightly compressed, adds even harmonics, glues elements together
when_to_use: Adding vintage character to digital sounds
tips: Push Pre to 40-50% for more obvious warmth
Combine with Master Filter Low Pass for vintage vibe
Works great on Rhodes, Wurlitzer, and organ sounds
presets.before_after: Before: Crisp, digital. After: Warm, slightly compressed, cohesive

presets.name: Hard Drive / Fuzz
presets.description: Heavy distortion that obliterates dynamics for maximum loudness.
presets.sonic_character: Distorted, saturated, aggressive, adds odd harmonics, compressed
tips: Crank Pre to 100% for maximum destruction
Use High Pass filter before this to avoid mud
Combine with resonant filter for acid sounds
presets.before_after: Before: Clean bass. After: Aggressive, distorted, cuts through mix
presets.warning: Can be very loud - adjust mixer level accordingly

presets.name: Parallel Glue
presets.use_case: Drum Loops, Pluck Chords, Dynamic Layers
presets.description: Mixes a heavily compressed signal with the clean signal for punch + transients.
presets.sonic_character: Punchy transients with added body and sustain
when_to_use: Adding body to drums without losing punch
tips: Mix at 30-50% for best results
Too much Mix loses transients
Great on chord stabs and plucks
presets.before_after: Before: Punchy but thin. After: Punchy AND thick

presets.name: Lo-Fi Crush
tips: Low Mix (20-30%) works best
Combine with Master Filter Low Pass @ 3-5kHz
Add noise/vinyl crackle macros if available
presets.before_after: Before: Clean, digital. After: Degraded, vintage, lo-fi

presets.name: Vocal Shine
presets.description: Gentle compression that brings vocals/leads forward without harshness.
when_to_use: Lead synths that need to cut through
tips: Keep Pre moderate (20-30%)
Too much Pre causes harshness
Combine with short reverb for depth
presets.before_after: Before: Buried in mix. After: Upfront and present

presets.name: Soft Tape Saturation
presets.description: Emulates analog tape saturation with soft knee compression.
presets.sonic_character: Smooth, analog, glues elements, adds weight
when_to_use: Adding analog character to full arrangements
tips: Use on busses/groups rather than individual sounds
Mix at 70-90% for tape blend
Pair with vintage-style reverbs
presets.before_after: Before: Clean but separate elements. After: Cohesive, warm, analog

presets.name: Aggressive Pump
presets.use_case: EDM Leads, Synth Stabs, High-Energy Elements
presets.description: Hard compression for maximum impact and energy.
tips: Reduce Pre if it clips (causing artifacts)
Works great with bright, cutting sounds
May need to reduce mixer level
presets.before_after: Before: Dynamic. After: Compressed, loud, aggressive
presets.warning: Very aggressive - can cause ear fatigue

presets.name: Subtle Enhancement
presets.description: Barely-there warmth that adds polish without obvious processing.
when_to_use: When you need transparency with slight warmth
tips: Very subtle - A/B test to hear difference
Don't push Pre above 20%
Great for adding "glue" without coloration
presets.before_after: Before: Pristine. After: Slightly more cohesive

presets.name: Bass Thickener
presets.description: Adds weight and harmonics to bass sounds without losing punch.
presets.sonic_character: Thick, punchy, adds harmonics for clarity on small speakers
when_to_use: Sub bass that disappears on laptop speakers
tips: Check in mono - bass should stay tight
Combine with Distortion type for aggressive bass
Keep bass completely dry (0% reverb)
presets.before_after: Before: Clean but thin bass. After: Thick, punchy, audible on all systems

workflow_tips: Start with 'Transparent Safety' and only add character if needed
Use Heating/Distortion for aggressive electronic genres
Always A/B test - your ears might be fatigued
common_mistakes: Using Distortion on everything - causes ear fatigue
Not adjusting mixer level after heavy limiting
Forgetting to check mono compatibility after saturation
Too much Pre causing unwanted clipping artifacts

macroArchetypes.description: Reusable configurations for Macros and Master FX to achieve specific sound characters. Since FLEX oscillators are fixed, these archetypes focus on shaping.

filterCurves.description: Configuration recipes for FLEX's Master Filter (Bottom Left) to create mixing tools and special effects.

filter_types_explained.Low Pass: Removes high frequencies - makes sound darker/warmer
filter_types_explained.High Pass: Removes low frequencies - makes sound thinner/cleaner
filter_types_explained.Band Pass: Only allows middle frequencies - telephone/radio effect
filter_types_explained.Notch: Removes a specific frequency band - surgical cut
filter_types_explained.Peak: Boosts a specific frequency band - emphasis
filter_types_explained.Phaser: Creates sweeping phase cancellation - psychedelic effect
filter_types_explained.All Pass: Changes phase without affecting frequency - subtle structural changes

curves.name: The Clean-Up (High Pass)
curves.description: Removes unnecessary low frequencies from non-bass instruments.
curves.sonic_character: Cleaner, tighter, removes mud and rumble
when_to_use: Pads to make room for bass
Removing rumble from any non-bass sound
automation_ideas: Start at 80Hz, sweep to 200Hz during build-ups
tips: Sweep up until sound gets thin, then back off slightly
Be careful with pianos - don't cut too much
Use 6dB slope for gentle cut, 24dB for aggressive
curves.before_after: Before: Muddy, competing with bass. After: Clean, clear, focused

curves.name: Telephone / Radio
curves.description: Isolates the midrange for a lo-fi communication device sound.
curves.sonic_character: Thin, nasal, lo-fi, vintage communication device
when_to_use: Intro effects before full sound drops
automation_ideas: Automate from Band Pass to Off (bypass) for dramatic reveal
Sweep cutoff 800Hz to 3kHz for scanning radio effect
tips: Combine with bit crusher or distortion for more degradation
Works great on vocals and keys
Lower cutoff (800Hz) = older phone, higher (2kHz) = modern
curves.before_after: Before: Full range. After: Tinny, narrow, vintage

curves.name: Acid Squelch
automation_ideas: CRITICAL: Automate cutoff constantly - static acid is boring
Fast cutoff sweeps (16th notes) for classic acid
Slow sweeps for building tension
tips: High resonance (70-90%) is essential
24dB slope is critical for authentic sound
Combine with Limiter 'Distortion' for more grit
curves.before_after: Before: Static bass. After: Squelchy, animated, aggressive
curves.warning: High resonance can cause piercing frequencies - watch levels

curves.name: Talkbox Vowel
curves.description: Imparts a vocal quality to the sound through formant filtering.
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff 0-100% = cycles through vowel sounds (A-E-I-O-U)
Step automation for rhythmic talking effect
Slow sweep for evolving vocal character
tips: Move cutoff slowly to hear different vowels
Works best on harmonically rich sounds
Combine with slight distortion for more character
curves.before_after: Before: Normal synth. After: Sounds like it's singing/talking

curves.name: Phaser Wash
curves.description: Adds swirling phase cancellation movement to static sounds.
automation_ideas: Sine wave automation on cutoff for classic phaser sweep
Increase resonance during builds for more intensity
Random LFO for unpredictable movement
tips: Phaser 1 = subtle, Phaser 2 = medium, Phaser 3 = intense
Higher resonance = more pronounced effect
Use slow automation (4-8 bars) for best results
curves.before_after: Before: Static. After: Swirling, moving, spacey

curves.name: Anti-Fizz (Low Pass)
curves.description: Tames harsh digital high frequencies without muffling the sound.
curves.sonic_character: Smoother highs, less digital harshness, more analog feel
when_to_use: Bright sawtooth synths that are too harsh
Presets with too much high-end sizzle
automation_ideas: Open up to 12kHz during chorus/drop for more energy
Close down to 6kHz for verses/quieter sections
tips: 6dB slope is key - gentle and natural
Don't go below 7kHz or sound gets muffled
Use instead of EQ for more natural sound
curves.before_after: Before: Harsh, digital, fatiguing. After: Smooth, warm, pleasant

curves.name: Sub Bass Isolator
curves.description: Removes everything except sub frequencies for powerful low end.
curves.sonic_character: Pure sub bass, no harmonics, floor-shaking
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff from 80Hz to 200Hz for bass that growls up
tips: Keep this layer MONO - critical for club systems
Layer with mid bass (200Hz+) for complete bass sound
Use 24dB slope for clean cutoff
curves.before_after: Before: Full bass. After: Pure sub frequencies only

curves.name: Air Filter (High Shelf)
curves.description: Simulates high shelf EQ for adding air and presence.
automation_ideas: Increase resonance to 50% during chorus for lift
tips: Don't overdo it - can get harsh quickly
Works best on already-bright sounds
Combine with Limiter 'Warming' to control harshness
curves.before_after: Before: Dull. After: Bright, airy, sparkly

curves.name: Notch Sweep
curves.description: Sweeping notch creates dramatic movement and tension.
automation_ideas: Sweep from low to high over 8 bars for build-up
Fast sweeps (1 bar) for dramatic effect
Step automation for glitchy sounds
tips: High resonance makes the sweep more obvious
Works great on white noise and full mixes
Combine with reverb automation for bigger effect
curves.before_after: Before: Static. After: Sweeping, moving, dramatic

curves.name: Comb Metallic
curves.description: Creates metallic, robotic, or alien-like sounds through comb filtering.
curves.frequency_target: Creates series of notches for metallic quality
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff for tuned metallic notes
Subtle movement adds character
tips: Comb+ and Comb- sound different - try both
Works best on harmonically rich sounds
Small cutoff movements create big changes
curves.before_after: Before: Normal synth. After: Metallic, robotic, unusual

curves.name: Lo-Fi Muffler
curves.description: Aggressive low pass for heavy lo-fi character.
automation_ideas: Automate from 1kHz to 8kHz for dramatic open-up
Keep low during verses, open for chorus
tips: Combine with Limiter 'Warming' for vintage sound
Lower cutoff (1-2kHz) for extreme lo-fi
Add noise/crackle macros if available
curves.before_after: Before: Modern, bright. After: Vintage, muffled, nostalgic

workflow_tips: Start with Master Filter OFF - only add if needed
Static filters are for mixing, animated filters are for effects
High Pass everything except bass and kick
Low Pass to remove digital harshness
automation_workflow: 1. Right-click Cutoff knob → Create automation clip
2. Draw your automation curve (sweeps, steps, etc.)
3. Adjust Resonance for more dramatic sweeps
4. A/B test to ensure it's not too extreme
common_mistakes: Too much high pass - sound gets thin
Too much low pass - sound gets muffled
Forgetting to automate - filter just sits there
Too much resonance - causes painful peaks
Using steep slopes when gentle would work better

genre_quick_reference.Drops: Low Pass @ 8kHz, open to full during drop

flex-params.description: Preset-based synthesizer with Subtractive, Wavetable, Multisample, FM & AM synthesis engines. Over 50GB of content across multiple expansion packs.

interface_sections.bottom: Master FX Chain (Filter, Delay, Reverb, Limiter)

parameters.name: Macros 1-8
parameters.description: Custom meta-controls specific to each preset. One macro often controls 10+ underlying parameters simultaneously.
tips: Automate these to transform the sound completely
Lock macros (show panel locks) to keep settings when browsing presets
These are the most powerful controls in FLEX
automation_ideas: Slow automation (4-8 bars) for evolving textures
Fast automation (1/16 notes) for wobble bass
Step automation for rhythmic gating
Envelope-triggered for dynamic response

parameters.name: Cutoff
parameters.label: Filter Cutoff
parameters.description: Controls the brightness by filtering frequencies above (Low Pass) or below (High Pass) the cutoff point.
parameters.parameter_interaction: Affected by Env Amt (envelope modulation) and often linked to Macro 1
tips: Automate for 'wobble' bass effects
Lower for darker, warmer sounds
Higher for brighter, more aggressive sounds
Works in conjunction with Master Filter
automation_ideas: Slow upward sweep for filter builds
Fast LFO for wobble bass (Dubstep)
Envelope-triggered for dynamic plucks

parameters.name: Resonance
parameters.label: Filter Resonance / Q
parameters.description: Boosts frequencies around the cutoff point, creating emphasis and 'squelch'.
parameters.parameter_interaction: Works with Cutoff - high resonance with low cutoff = bass emphasis
tips: High resonance (70-90%) creates 'squelchy' acid textures
Medium (30-50%) adds character without harshness
0% for clean, transparent filtering
Can cause self-oscillation at very high values
parameters.warning: Very high resonance can create loud, piercing frequencies - monitor levels

parameters.name: Env Amt
parameters.label: Envelope Amount
parameters.description: Controls how much the envelope modulates the filter cutoff.
parameters.parameter_interaction: Uses the same envelope as volume (AHDSR)
tips: Positive values: Filter opens from low to high (wah effect)
Negative values: Filter closes from high to low (ow effect)
Higher values = more dramatic movement
Combine with resonance for pronounced effects

parameters.name: Attack (A)
parameters.label: Envelope Attack
parameters.description: Time from 0% to 100% volume/brightness after key press.
parameters.parameter_interaction: Affects both volume and filter cutoff (if Env Amt is set)
tips: 0% = Instant (percussion, plucks, bass)
25-50% = Natural swell (strings, brass)
70-90% = Slow fade-in (pads, ambience)
Add 2-5% if you hear clicks at note start

parameters.name: Hold (H)
parameters.label: Envelope Hold
parameters.description: Time at peak level before decay starts.
tips: Short hold (0-10%) for most sounds
Medium hold (20-40%) for percussive elements with body
Long hold (50%+) for organ-like sustained attack

parameters.name: Decay (D)
parameters.label: Envelope Decay
parameters.description: Time from peak level down to sustain level.
tips: Short decay (10-30%) for punchy sounds
Medium decay (40-60%) for natural decay
Long decay (70%+) for slow transitions

parameters.name: Sustain (S)
parameters.label: Envelope Sustain
parameters.description: Volume level maintained while key is held (after decay phase).
parameters.parameter_interaction: This is a LEVEL, not a time. 100% = full volume, 0% = silent
tips: 100% for pads and sustained sounds
0% for plucks and percussion (one-shot sounds)
50-80% for piano-like decay
Lower sustain if sound is too loud when held

parameters.name: Release (R)
parameters.label: Envelope Release
parameters.description: Time from current level to 0% after key release.
tips: Short release (5-15%) for tight, punchy sounds (808s)
Medium release (30-50%) for natural decay (strings)
Long release (70-90%) for atmospheric tails (pads)
Reduce release if notes overlap and muddy the mix
parameters.warning: Very long releases can cause CPU buildup with complex chords

parameters.name: Master Filter Type
parameters.label: Master Filter Type Selector
parameters.description: Global filter applied to the final output. Different algorithms for mixing and creative effects.
tips: Use High Pass 12dB @ 150-200Hz for de-mudding non-bass sounds
Low Pass for vintage/lo-fi character
Vowel/Phaser for creative effects
24dB slopes are steeper/more aggressive

parameters.name: Master Filter Cutoff
parameters.label: Master Filter Frequency
parameters.description: Sets the frequency point for the Master Filter.
tips: Automate for dramatic filter sweeps
Critical parameter for build-ups and drops

parameters.name: Master Filter Resonance
parameters.label: Master Filter Q/Resonance
parameters.description: Resonance/emphasis for the Master Filter.
tips: High values (70-90%) for acid effects
Keep at 0% for clean mixing filters

parameters.name: Delay Type
parameters.label: Delay Mode Selector
parameters.description: Delay algorithm type affecting stereo behavior.

option_details.Fake Stereo: Haas effect - very short L/R offset for widening
option_details.True Stereo: Independent L/R delays - preserves stereo image
option_details.Ping Pong: Bounces between left and right channels

tips: Fake Stereo for widening mono sounds (10-25ms)
True Stereo for maintaining stereo presets
Ping Pong for rhythmic, spatial effects

parameters.name: Delay Time
parameters.label: Delay Time/Sync
parameters.description: Time between delay repeats. Can be free-running or tempo-synced.
tips: Use tempo-sync for rhythmic delays
Use free time (ms) for slapback and Haas effects
Dotted times (1/4 Dot, 1/8 Dot) sound more musical

parameters.name: Delay Feedback
parameters.label: Delay Feedback/Repeats
parameters.description: Amount of delay output fed back into input - controls number of echoes.
tips: 0-30% = Single or few repeats
40-60% = Multiple echoes
70-90% = Many repeats, near-infinite
100%+ = Infinite feedback (use carefully)
parameters.warning: Feedback above 85% can create runaway feedback - automate carefully
automation_ideas: Automate 30% to 80% during builds for dub effects

parameters.name: Delay Mix
parameters.label: Delay Wet/Dry Mix
parameters.description: Balance between dry (unprocessed) and wet (delayed) signal.
tips: 0% = No delay
15-30% = Subtle space
40-60% = Obvious rhythmic delay
Use lower values for mixing, higher for effects

parameters.name: Reverb Decay
parameters.label: Reverb Decay Time
parameters.description: Time for reverb tail to fade to silence.
tips: Short (0.5-1s) = Small room, tight
Medium (1.5-3s) = Studio, natural
Long (4s+) = Hall, cathedral, epic
Faster tempos need shorter decay to avoid mud

parameters.name: Reverb Size
parameters.label: Reverb Room Size
parameters.description: Simulated room/space size.
tips: Small (10-30%) = Tight room, intimate
Medium (40-60%) = Studio, natural
Large (70-100%) = Hall, epic, huge

parameters.name: Reverb Mix
parameters.label: Reverb Wet/Dry Mix
parameters.description: Balance between dry and reverb signal.
tips: 0% = Completely dry
10-20% = Subtle ambience
30-50% = Obvious space
60%+ = Washed out, very wet
NEVER use reverb on bass/808s
common_mistakes: Too much reverb muddies the mix
Using reverb on bass destroys low-end clarity
Same reverb amount on all presets - be dynamic

parameters.name: Reverb Color
parameters.label: Reverb Tone/Brightness
parameters.description: Tone/brightness of the reverb tail.
tips: 0-30% = Dark, warm, vintage
40-60% = Neutral, natural
70-100% = Bright, airy, modern
Match color to genre - dark for lo-fi, bright for EDM

parameters.name: Reverb Mod
parameters.label: Reverb Modulation
parameters.description: Adds pitch modulation/chorus to reverb tail.
tips: 0% = Clean, metallic reverb
20-40% = Removes metallic ringing
60%+ = Chorus/shimmer effect
Use to add movement to static pads

parameters.name: Limiter Type
parameters.label: Limiter Mode
parameters.description: Limiting/compression algorithm with different saturation colors.
tips: Limiter for clean, digital production
Warming for analog warmth and glue
Heating for aggressive punch
Distortion for maximum aggression (808s, bass)

parameters.name: Limiter Pre
parameters.label: Limiter Pre-Gain
parameters.description: Input gain into the limiter section. Drives saturation/distortion.
tips: 0% = No coloration
20-40% = Subtle warmth (Warming mode)
50-70% = Obvious saturation
80-100% = Heavy distortion
Adjust based on Limiter Type
parameters.warning: High Pre gain can cause clipping - reduce mixer level if needed

parameters.name: Master Volume
parameters.label: Output Level
parameters.description: Final output level before FL Studio mixer.
tips: Lock this (padlock icon) to maintain consistent volume when browsing presets
Reduce if preset is too loud
Usually set once and locked

parameters.name: Pitch
parameters.label: Fine Tune
parameters.description: Fine pitch tuning in cents (100 cents = 1 semitone).
tips: ±10-15 cents for slight detuning between layers
±50 cents for experimental detuning
Use for matching presets to out-of-tune samples

parameters.name: Arpeggiator Icon
parameters.label: Arpeggiator Toggle
parameters.description: Enables/disables built-in arpeggiator or sequencer for preset.
tips: Orange = Arpeggiator is active
Click to toggle on/off
If preset has unwanted rhythm, turn this off

parameters.name: Dump Score Icon
parameters.label: Extract MIDI
parameters.description: Extracts MIDI notes from loop-based presets to Piano Roll.
tips: Only available on presets with embedded MIDI
Click to dump notes to active pattern
Use for learning, variation, or layering

common_problems.solution: Click the 'Arpeggiator' icon (pyramid of dots) in the pitch section to disable the built-in arp.
common_problems.visual_indicator: Icon changes from Orange (on) to Grey (off)

common_problems.symptom: Sound never stops playing / Long tail
common_problems.solution: Reduce the 'R' (Release) slider in the Volume Envelope section to 5-15%.
additional_checks: Check Reverb Mix - high reverb can extend tails
Check Delay Feedback - high feedback creates infinite echoes

common_problems.solution: Increase the 'Master Volume' slider (bottom right) or 'Limiter Pre' gain (10-30%).
alternative_solutions: Check if Macros are turned down
Check if preset has very low sustain level

common_problems.solution: Reduce Master Volume or Limiter Pre gain. Check for red clipping indicators.
common_problems.prevention: Lock Master Volume at comfortable level when browsing presets

common_problems.symptom: Sound is too wet / washed out / drowning in reverb
common_problems.solution: Lower Reverb Mix to 0-20% and Delay Mix to 0-20%. Check Macros 5-8 which often control effects.
common_problems.additional_tip: Lock these knobs if you want to browse with consistent wetness

common_problems.symptom: Sound is too bright / harsh / piercing
common_problems.solution: Lower Filter Cutoff, or enable Master Filter 'Low Pass 12dB' at 8-10kHz. Check Macro 1 (often brightness).
additional_solutions: Reduce Filter Resonance if set high
Use Limiter 'Warming' instead of 'Limiter' for softer highs

common_problems.symptom: Sound is too dark / muffled / dull
common_problems.solution: Increase Filter Cutoff to 70-90%, or check if Master Filter Low Pass is enabled (disable it).
additional_checks: Ensure Env Amt isn't set to negative with fast attack

common_problems.symptom: Click or pop at note start
common_problems.solution: Increase Attack slider slightly (2-5%) to soften the transient.
alternative_causes: Limiter Pre too high causing clipping

common_problems.symptom: Bass sounds too wide / loses power in mono
common_problems.solution: Check Vectorscope - should be vertical line. Lower 'Width' or 'Unison' Macros. Use mixer stereo separation at 0% for bass.
common_problems.prevention: Always check bass sounds in mono
common_problems.critical: Wide bass causes phase cancellation on club systems

common_problems.symptom: CPU usage too high / Audio glitches
common_problems.solution: Check for 'Unison' or 'Voices' Macros and reduce them. Increase FL Studio buffer size. Freeze/render track.
additional_solutions: Render to audio if performance critical

common_problems.solution: Reduce Release time to 10-20%. For bass, keep at 5-10%.
additional_checks: Use High Pass filter on non-bass elements

common_problems.solution: Some parameters were locked. Click FLEX logo → uncheck 'Show panel locks' or unlock individual padlock icons.
common_problems.note: This is actually a feature - use locks intentionally to maintain settings

common_problems.solution: The 'Dump Score' icon is grey, meaning this preset has no embedded MIDI data. Only loop-based presets support MIDI extraction.
common_problems.workaround: Record the audio and use melody detection, or play it manually

common_problems.solution: Check Env Amt knob - if set high (positive or negative), it's modulating the filter. Set to 0% for static filter.
additional_checks: Check if Macro is controlling filter cutoff
Look for automation on Filter Cutoff

common_problems.symptom: Sound cuts off before MIDI note ends
common_problems.solution: Increase Sustain level to 80-100%, or check if Decay is too short with 0% Sustain (causes one-shot behavior).
common_problems.note: Some presets intentionally use 0% Sustain for pluck/percussion sounds

workflow_best_practices: Lock Master Volume when browsing presets to maintain consistent loudness
Always check bass sounds with Vectorscope - should be mono (vertical line)
Use Alt + Click on Macros to reset to designer's intended default
Automate Macros for movement - static presets sound boring
Check mono compatibility before exporting - especially on bass
Use 'Show panel locks' feature to keep reverb/volume consistent while browsing
Start with Limiter 'Limiter' mode, only add color if needed
High Pass filter everything except kick and bass
Use short Attack times for rhythmic elements, long for pads

keyboard_shortcuts.shortcut: Double-Click FLEX logo or Analysis display

cpu_optimization: Increase buffer size in FL Studio settings

rules.description: The sound is drowning in reverb or delay, losing its definition.

recommendations.notes: Turn down the Reverb Mix knob in the bottom effects row.
Turn down the Delay Mix knob. Also check if Macro sliders 5-8 are controlling FX levels.

rules.description: After releasing the key, the sound continues for too long (long release tail).

recommendations.notes: Drag the 'R' slider in the Volume Envelope section downwards to shorten the fade-out time.

rules.description: The preset plays a sequence or pattern instead of a sustained note.

recommendations.notes: Click the pyramid-of-dots icon in the Pitch section. If it's orange, the arp is active. Click to turn it grey.

rules.description: The high frequencies are piercing or fatiguing.

recommendations.notes: Turn down the main Filter Cutoff knob. Also check Macro 1, which often controls brightness.
Enable the Master Filter (bottom left) and set it to 'LP 12dB' to roll off highs.

rules.description: FLEX is causing audio glitches or high CPU load.

recommendations.notes: Check if any Macro controls 'Unison' or 'Voices' and turn it down.
Increase your audio buffer size in FL Studio settings.
